sidebar-accent.purpose: The current nav item, the current counts cut's pill, an active filter trigger, and the keyboard cursor row.

badge-green-solid.purpose: The only solid-filled badge in the app: the Status the whole search is for.

selection.purpose: ::selection background; the browser's own surface, themed rather than left at default.

chart-1.purpose: Defined and unrendered. Walks the accent out towards the canvas so the first chart inherits the app's one colour.

page-title.purpose: The one h1 per page, in the white header band, plus the empty state heading. Text-balanced.

dialog-title.purpose: Overlay headings only. Medium weight, not semibold.

body.purpose: Table cells, form fields, dialog copy. The working size of the app.

interface.purpose: Nav items, counts-row cuts, back links. Always medium weight, so chrome reads as chrome.

meta.purpose: Stacked mobile row second line, account email, count pills, the Status badge's word.

label-micro.purpose: Every small uppercase label: table column heads, field labels, section labels. Defined once as .label-micro so tracking never drifts. Never a kicker above a page title.

numeric.purpose: A treatment, not a size. Tabular figures forced on every table and anything [data-numeric].

fonts.purpose: The only typeface in the app. No display face, no mono. --font-heading resolves to the same family.

shadows.name: shadow-xs
shadows.purpose: Bevel, not elevation: buttons, inputs, select triggers, keycaps.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Smallest true lift. Defined; used on the account panel only.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Defined and currently unused. Not a role in the shipped system.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Menu lift: the select popover and the Company suggestion list.

shadows.name: shadow-xl
shadows.purpose: Overlay lift: the dialog and the mobile drawer, the two things that cover the app.

shadows.name: shadow-near
shadows.purpose: Near alpha layer. Deepens in dark, where a shadow has less contrast to work with.

shadows.name: shadow-far
shadows.purpose: Far alpha layer. Every shadow is these two tokens, stacked.

motion.name: status-set
motion.value: status-set 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both — from { opacity: 0; transform: scale(1.12); filter: blur(2px) } to { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); filter: blur(0) }
motion.purpose: The one authored moment in the app. Fires only on a Status badge whose Status has actually just changed; off on mount, off inside an open Status list, off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: blur-in
motion.value: blur-in 0.5s ease-out both — from { opacity: 0; filter: blur(8px); transform: translateY(0.4rem) } to { opacity: 1; filter: blur(0); transform: translateY(0) }
motion.purpose: The empty state's heading resolves out of blur. The only decorative animation, on the one screen with nothing to do.

motion.name: overlay-enter
motion.purpose: Dialog and select popover. Suppressed when a select aligns an item to its trigger.

motion.name: drawer-enter
motion.purpose: The mobile navigation drawer and its backdrop fade.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The one tactile cue. Applies to every button that is not a popup trigger.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Company column appears; gutters widen to 1.5rem; count pills take their fill; the scrolling rails and their .fade-end mask dissolve.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Source and Last change columns appear; input type drops from 16px to 14px.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: The 15rem sidebar column appears and the mobile header plus drawer disappear.

layout.shell: lg+: grid [15rem minmax(0,1fr)] with a sticky full-height sidebar. Below lg: a 3.5rem sticky header and a 17rem (max 85vw) left drawer holding the identical AppSidebar.
layout.gutter: px-4 sm:px-6 — shared by the header band, the counts row, the working area and the empty state.
layout.density: 36px column heads, 44px table rows, 32px default controls, 20px badges, 3.5rem chrome bars.
layout.columnSlack: Role 30% / Company 22%, both truncating, so neither hoards the table's slack.

narrative.overview:
This is the category standard played straight at the craft level of the Stripe dashboard — the single reference product the owner named, chosen deliberately over every more expressive alternative. There is no irony here and no smuggled quirk. A 240px panel of navigation stands against a cool grey canvas; white panels sit on that canvas, divided by hairlines; ink is a navy (#1A1F36), never pure black; one violet accent (#635BFF) carries every primary action, every active nav state, the focus ring and the text caret. Everything else that carries meaning is a Status.

The identity has to come from type, colour, layout and motion that ship in code, because there is no logo asset, no licensed typeface and no illustration budget. So it does: the mark is a drawn SVG of two list rows with the lower one current, the typeface is one self-hosted variable face used at every size, and the colour system is the nine-value Status vocabulary rather than a decorative palette. The table is the product. Density is high and deliberate — 44px rows, 36px column heads, 11px uppercase column labels, tabular numerals wherever anything is compared down a column — and the hierarchy is bought with weight and colour rather than with size, so the whole working surface stays inside a narrow type ramp.

Both themes are first-class. The app follows the device by default, remembers an override, and applies the resolved theme before first paint so it never flashes the wrong one. Neither theme is a filter over the other: each has its own hand-picked hex for every token, including nine Status pairs tuned separately for a light canvas and a dark one. Depth is rationed: shadows mean "this floats above the page", and nothing on the canvas floats.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, one typeface, nine semantic Status pairs — and nothing else carrying colour meaning.
Hairlines, not shadows, divide the working surface.
Small radii (6px base), 4px on chips and badges.
Dense tables with tabular numerals and an 11px uppercase column label.
Light and dark both authored by hand, system-followed, override persisted, no flash.
Exactly one authored motion moment in the whole app.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: #635BFF is the only accent the app has. Primary action, current nav, current cut, focus ring, caret, brand mark, first chart step — all of it is this one violet. A new surface that needs to mean something uses a Status pair or a neutral step; it does not introduce a second accent hue.

rules.name: The Status Vocabulary Is The Palette Rule
rules.body: Semantic colour comes from the eight Status pairs and nowhere else. A new state that is not a Status does not get a new colour; it gets type weight, a neutral step, or a border.

rules.name: The 4.5 Floor Rule
rules.body: Every foreground/background pair in the system clears 4.5:1 in both themes, verified by computation over all 32 pairs. A visual effect that would push a pair under the floor loses to the floor.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Geist Variable is the only typeface. No second face, no mono costume, no system display font, and no webfont loaded from a third party.

rules.name: The Narrow Ramp Rule
rules.body: The whole app lives between 11px and 20px. Hierarchy is bought with weight (400 / 500 / 600) and colour (ink versus quiet ink), not with size. A new surface that wants emphasis reaches for 600 weight before it reaches for a bigger size.

rules.name: The Tabular Column Rule
rules.body: Anything compared down a column — counts, days-since, dates — is tabular. Use the table element or mark the element [data-numeric]; do not re-declare the font feature locally.

rules.name: The Glossary Word Rule
rules.body: Every Status, Source and filter is written with its GLOSSARY.md word, capitalised as a domain noun. Colour, position and iconography are all additions to the word, never replacements for it.

rules.name: The Shared Gutter Rule
rules.body: px-4 sm:px-6, everywhere on a page. Header band, counts row, working area and empty state all use it, so every left edge on the page is the same left edge.

rules.name: The No Information Loss Rule
rules.body: A narrow viewport may remove a column, never a fact. Whatever a hidden column would have said moves into the row's second line.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Panels on the canvas separate by a 1px hairline, never by a shadow. If a surface is not floating over the app, it has no shadow.

rules.name: The Float Earns The Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow is a claim that the element is above the page and the page is beneath it. Dialog, select popover, mobile drawer. Nothing else.

rules.name: The Two Soft Layers Rule
rules.body: Shadows are always two stacked soft layers off the --shadow-near / --shadow-far alpha tokens, so they re-tune per theme. No single-layer shadow, no hard offset shadow, no coloured shadow.

rules.name: The Small Radius Rule
rules.body: 6px is the house radius and nothing on the working surface exceeds it except the dialog. Pills are for dots, avatars and scrollbars only; a pill-shaped button or badge is out of world.

rules.name: The Word And The Dot Rule
rules.body: A Status is always colour plus its glossary word plus a dot. Colour is never the only carrier of a Status — it is a hard accessibility floor, not a stylistic preference.

rules.name: The One Authored Moment Rule
rules.body: The app has exactly one expressive animation, and it is attached to the single event the product is about: a Status changing. Adding a second expressive moment devalues it. Every animation, decorative or not, has a prefers-reduced-motion answer.

dos: Do take every colour from packages/web/src/index.css, and add new colours as a token in both :root and .dark before using them. The stylesheet is the single source of truth for the palette.
Do give any new foreground/background pair a measured contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 in both themes before it ships.
Do separate panels on the canvas with a 1px border hairline and the canvas-to-panel colour step.
Do reserve shadows for the three things that float: dialog, select popover, mobile drawer.
Do use .label-micro for every small uppercase label rather than re-declaring 11px uppercase tracking locally.
Do write every Status, Source and filter with its GLOSSARY.md word, and pair any colour-coded state with that word and a shape (the dot).
Do mark anything compared down a column [data-numeric], or put it in a table, so it is tabular.
Do keep the house radius at 6px and use the literal 4px only for badge-scale objects.
Do give every new control a keyboard path and a visible :focus-visible treatment — 3px ring/50 on form controls, a 2px inset ring where there is no room outside.
Do keep an unbuilt view in the navigation with a Soon chip and a title naming what it will hold, rather than hiding it and letting the nav rearrange later.
Do keep information when a column is dropped at a narrow width: move it into the row's second line.
Do author light and dark as two first-class themes, and apply the resolved theme before first paint.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue. The primary violet carries every primary action, active state, ring and caret.
Don't invent a colour for a state that is not a Status. Use a Status pair, a neutral step, type weight, or a border.
Don't let colour be the only carrier of a Status, a filter state, or a Ghosted marker.
Don't put a shadow on a panel that sits on the canvas.
Don't use a single-layer, hard-offset, or coloured shadow; shadows are two soft layers off --shadow-near / --shadow-far.
Don't add a second typeface — no display face, no mono, no system font stack as a deliberate choice, no third-party webfont.
Don't exceed 20px type on a working surface, or reach for a bigger size where 600 weight would do.
Don't use pill radii on buttons or badges. Pills are for dots, avatars, scrollbars and skeleton bars.
Don't add a second expressive animation. status-set is the app's one authored moment.
Don't ship an animation without a prefers-reduced-motion answer.
Don't use glyph, emoji or icon-font icons; icons are inline lucide SVG at 12–16px with aria-hidden, and an icon-only control always carries an aria-label.
Don't add an uppercase kicker or eyebrow line above a page title. .label-micro is for column heads, field labels and section labels; the page title stands alone above its meta line.
Don't trade a contrast ratio for a visual effect. The 4.5 floor outranks the effect, every time.
Don't leave the browser's own surfaces at their defaults: selection, caret, scrollbar and backdrop are themed here and new surfaces inherit them.
